item.title: About
item.description:
I am an AI/ML researcher and engineer interested in building intelligent systems.

My background spans computer engineering, machine learning for biology, large language models, and production AI systems.

I enjoy working at the boundary between research and engineering: turning ideas into systems that work in the real world.

Currently I work on applied AI systems in healthcare and explore new approaches to agents, evaluation, and learning.

item.title: Cell2Sentence
item.description:
Cell2Sentence explores how biological measurements can be represented as sequences that language models can process.

The project adapts LLM ideas to single-cell biology, connecting representation learning, natural language modeling, and biological discovery.

See the paper and code for technical details.

item.title: Evals Are the New Engineering Artifacts
item.description:
Traditional software relies on explicit specifications. AI systems increasingly require a different contract: the ability to measure whether behavior is good.

Evaluation becomes a core engineering artifact.

It defines what success means, creates feedback loops, and allows intelligent systems to improve.

item.title: How Much Can an Interview Actually Measure?
item.description:
Every evaluation system has limited resolution.

An interview, benchmark, or committee can only distinguish capabilities within the range it is designed to measure.

Understanding evaluator capacity is essential for building better selection systems.

item.title: Machine Learning for Protein Biology
item.description:
During my PhD, I worked on machine-learning methods that infer biological and structural properties directly from protein sequence.

The work covered several related problems: predicting intrinsically disordered regions and their functions, DNA-binding residues, protein-binding residues, crystal-structure quality, and sequence-derived signals associated with druggability.

A recurring theme was learning useful representations from sequence when direct structural evidence is sparse or unavailable. That meant thinking carefully about labels, evaluation, biological priors, and the gap between benchmark performance and useful scientific inference.

item.title: Patient Record Linkage at Scale
item.description:
Overview #

I designed and built a large-scale patient matching system combining learned representations with deterministic constraints.

The system used neural embeddings, blocking strategies, clustering, and precision/recall evaluation techniques to link records across healthcare datasets while balancing accuracy and scalability.

Why it matters #

Entity resolution is a foundation problem for healthcare data. Small errors have large downstream effects, and the system must combine statistical learning with domain knowledge.

item.title: The New Delegation Stack
item.description:
Computers historically automated only tasks with precisely specified procedures.

Large language models introduce a new layer: machines that can receive ambiguous goals, reason about approaches, and delegate work across different levels of intelligence and cost.

Future software architectures may dynamically allocate intelligence the way operating systems allocate compute.
